title: Warm-pool & prewarm orchestration for Dedicated: weight loading and KV cache priming
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Reduce cold-start impact for Dedicated capacity by introducing a warm-pool and prewarming orchestration for model weight loading and KV cache priming. Goal is to provide throughput guarantees and predictable latency during scale-ups and failover, while keeping incremental cost and tenant isolation constraints acceptable.

Problem: Dedicated customers occasionally observe large P95/P99 latency spikes and transient errors when the autoscaler attaches new workers or when workloads are routed to under-warmed GPUs. Root causes: 1) model weight file load times (I/O and memory allocation) and kernel/cuda initializations; 2) empty KV caches for chat/history workloads that must rebuild from client prompts (adds extra token-generation time and causes throughput variability); 3) runtime JIT/kernel warmups. These affect SLOs for bursty workloads and reduce confidence in throughput guarantees.

Proposal: Implement a warm-pool service in the Dedicated control plane with three coordinated capabilities:
1) Weight preloading: keep a configurable pool of idle workers with model weights loaded and runtime kernels initialized so attaching a worker is O(100ms) instead of O(seconds). We will support two modes: - host-preloaded (weights loaded into GPU memory resident) and - host-fast-load (weights cached on NVMe in optimized layout for fast mmap).
2) KV cache priming: allow tenants to provide (opt-in) representative prompt prefixes or use sampled production traffic to seed KV caches. Priming options: snapshot transfer (serialize KV shards from warmed workers), synthetic replay (replay representative prompts on prewarmed model instance), and predictive priming (populate likely prefixes based on historical telemetry).
3) Autoscaler integration and fleet controls: autoscaler will consult warm-pool size and prewarm budgets before scaling decisions. Provide policies: guaranteed-reserve (minimum n warm workers per pool), adaptive-target (scale warm pool proportionally to single-tenant 95th percentile QPS), and burst-provision (temporarily increase warm pool for scheduled events).

Design considerations and constraints:
- Tenant isolation: KV priming must never cross-tenant data boundaries. Any replay or snapshot must come from the same tenant or from anonymized synthetic prompts.
- Cost vs latency: warm workers incur reserved GPU-hours; product must balance SLA tiers (P0 customers get larger warm pools) and cost controls (max warm budget per-customer).
- Consistency with rollouts and upgrades: warm pool must support rolling model version updates and drain/replace semantics without traffic loss.
- Failure modes: stale KV snapshot causing degraded output quality; eviction of warm workers under memory pressure; prewarm overload causing scheduler congestion.

Telemetry and metrics to track:
- Cold-start latency P50/P95/P99 for new worker attach and for first-token latency after scale-up
- Time-to-ready weight-load median and 95th percentile
- KV cache hit rate before and after priming
- Throughput ramp slope (requests/sec per second) after scale events
- Cost delta: GPU-hours attributable to warm pool per tenant
- Number of primed snapshots and priming success/failure rate

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- Reduce cold-start P95 for new worker attach from baseline (currently ~6s) to <= 500ms for host-preloaded warm workers in 90% of events.
- KV cache hit-rate improvement of >=40% for primed tenants within 10 minutes of scale-up.
- No cross-tenant KV data movement; pass security audit checklist for priming flows.
- Warm-pool cost overhead <= 12% of monthly Dedicated spend for opt-in customers at default sizing.

Implementation plan (rough milestones):
1) Spike (1 week): measure realistic weight load times across supported instance types (A10, A100, H100) with optimized I/O layouts and quantify memory transient allocations. Create microbenchmarks.
2) Prototype weight preloader (2 weeks): implement a service that maintains N workers with weights loaded; expose attach API returning warmed worker IDs; measure attach latency reduction.
3) KV priming POC (3 weeks): build two priming flows - snapshot transfer and synthetic replay. Validate correctness and measure priming time and hit-rate improvements using historical tenant traces in staging.
4) Autoscaler integration (2 weeks): add policy hooks so autoscaler consults warm-pool and respects prewarm budgets; add controls to Console for pool sizing and policies.
5) Security review & tenancy hardening (1 week): ensure isolation, KMS handling for any persisted priming artifacts, and audit logs.
6) Canary rollout (2 weeks): expose to small set of Dedicated tenants with telemetry dashboards and opt-in flag.

Rollout plan: start with internal canary tenants (platform team), then early-adopter dedicated customers on invitation. Provide toggles for (a) weight-preload only, (b) weight + KV synthetic priming, (c) full snapshot-based priming. Monitor metrics for 2 weeks before broader enablement.

Operational playbooks:
- Warm-pool saturation: detect when warm-pool workers are depleted and automatically trigger a graceful scaling path with priority routing and fallback to best-compatible model variant.
- Failed priming: fallback to empty cache and mark tenant for manual review; do not retry more than N times per hour.
- Upgrade: drain warm workers, preload new model version into replacement workers, and swap atomically.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: KV priming accidentally stores PII across snapshot boundaries. Mitigation: require explicit tenant opt-in and scrub priming artifacts; require security review before enabling.
- Risk: Warm pool increases cost materially. Mitigation: adjustable budgets per-customer and dynamic shrink during low utilization windows.
- Risk: Primed KV mismatch leads to hallucination/regression. Mitigation: run eval suite on primed instance and require passing quality gates before allowing traffic.

Open questions: 
- Best default warm pool sizing heuristics for multi-tenant Dedicated hosts? (rule-of-thumb vs ML-based prediction)
- Should we support cross-model warm pools (same architecture compatible variants) to save memory?
- How to represent primed state in billing (meter warm hours vs amortize across requests)?

Docs and artifacts:

updates: 2026-03-02: Spike results - weight load times: A100 (80GB) median 4.8s, P95 6.3s using existing checkpoint layout; NVMe mmap layout reduces median to ~1.1s in lab with optimized serialization.

2026-03-04: Design review with PM (Priya Kapoor) and Security (Marcus Liu). Decided KV priming must be tenant-isolated; synthetic priming preferred for initial canary to avoid snapshot transfer complexity.
2026-03-06: Prototype weight preloader service bootstrapped in staging. Attach API returns warmed instance IDs and reduced attach time to ~180ms for hot path on A10 ensemble (still tuning).
2026-03-08: KV priming POC completed for synthetic replay. Using sampled prefix set from tenant traces increased early-token KV hit-rate from 8% to 55% in our chat workload test harness.
2026-03-10: Security questionnaire submitted. Requested clarification on long-term storage of priming artifacts and KMS envelope handling.
